subject: Provisional latency waiver & tiered credit cap — BlueHarbor pilot
messages:
From: Alice Ng <alice.ng@blueharbor.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@blueharbor.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot performance concerns and SLA ask

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the quick onboarding this week. Our pilot team has been exercising the model endpoints overnight and we're consistently seeing 95th percentile token latencies spike into the 950–1,200 ms range on several multi-turn workflows. That is causing a noticeable lag in our UI and a handful of timeouts in our orchestration layer.

We know this is a pilot and capacity is burstable, but our internal stakeholders require a temporary operational tolerance for latency while we tune prompts and routing. Specifically we're asking for: 
- A provisional latency SLO waiver for the pilot period (30 days) with a documented mitigation plan
- A cap on cumulative service credits at 10% of monthly bill for this pilot instead of the standard SLO credit formula

Attached are logs and a small SLO matrix for context. Can Redwood provide an executive-level signoff path for a negotiated waiver and reduced credit exposure? Procurement may need a formal note for our audit.

Appreciate any urgency here — the pilot goes live Mon at 9am PT.

Best,
Alice Ng
Sr. Platform Engineer | BlueHarbor Systems
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Alice Ng <alice.ng@blueharbor.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot performance concerns and SLA ask

Alice — thanks for the detail and the attachments. I pulled the overnight traces and Ben and I discussed the immediate mitigation steps (short term routing tweak + KV cache preload).

A few quick clarifications for our internal process: 
1) When you say "provisional waiver for 30 days", do you mean a full suspension of latency SLO credits or an explicit higher-latency threshold for the pilot?
2) The 10% credit cap — is that an absolute cap on dollars, or a cap relative to the pilot invoice?

I'll need exec concurrence for any deviation from our standard remedy formulas. Looping in Marissa and Ben to flag this to deal desk and request an expedited exec review.

I'll schedule a 30-minute sync for first thing Monday so we have concrete signoff before your production cutover.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 26 Jun 2027 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Pilot performance concerns and SLA ask

Team — forwarding BlueHarbor's ask. Quick summary from infra: spikes align with multi-region routing bouncing to fallback variant; cache warm-up is inconsistent for long context. We can implement an on-deploy warm cache + limit concurrent long-sequence sessions which should reduce the 95p by ~30–40%.

Commercial ask: BlueHarbor requests a 30-day elevated latency threshold and an alternative credit cap set to 10% of the pilot invoice (they estimate $28k/month pilot, so cap ~= $2.8k). From a risk standpoint, that's reasonable for a 30-day pilot if we get commitments: 
- engineering remediation timeline (we provide)
- explicit rollback to standard SLOs after 30 days
- no upstream SLA obligations in integrations that require stricter latency

Marissa — can you advise whether this is in-scope for expedited deal desk approval or needs exec signoff? If exec, suggest we ask for a single point of contact and a short memo for approval.

—Ben
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 08:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot performance concerns and SLA ask

Kimberly/Ben — I'm flagging this to the deal desk for exception handling. Per our policy, any deviation that changes the remedy calculation or the monetary exposure requires an executive approval unless confined to an internal pilot < $5k/mo exposure. BlueHarbor's estimated exposure (~$2.8k) is under that threshold but they requested a formal cap in contract language which is non-standard.

Proposal for exec note (short): 
- Approve a provisional latency threshold increase to 900ms 95p for 30 days for BH-2345 pilot only
- Approve a capped cumulative service credit of 10% of the pilot invoice for the same period (estimated cap $2.8k)
- Condition: Redwood engineering provides the remediation plan with milestones and daily check-ins; rollback to standard SLOs at day 31

If we get signoff, I'll draft the short amendment and send to procurement. Requesting approval from either: CFO (finance@redwood.com) or Head of Sales Ops (exec@redwood.com) — who can sign under 24 hours?

Marissa
Head of Deal Desk | Redwood Inference
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Re: Pilot performance concerns and SLA ask — Exec approver identified

Marissa/Kim — quick update: CFO has delegated signoff to Sales Ops for pilot exceptions under $5k exposure. Sales Ops (exec@redwood.com) approved the three bullet memo below and asked Legal to issue a one-paragraph amendment.

Executive approval (verbatim):
"Approved: provisional 95p latency threshold of 900ms for a maximum of 30 days for account BH-2345 (BlueHarbor Systems). Cumulative service-credit liability for the pilot is capped at 10% of the pilot invoice. Approval conditioned on remediation milestones and automatic reversion to standard SLOs at day 31."

Action items completed: 
- Marissa: please draft the amendment and route to procurement@blueharbor.com + Alice
- Ben/Infra: send the remediation plan and daily health report schedule by EOD
- Kimberly: confirm pilot cutover schedule still Monday 9am PT

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
VP, Sales Ops (on behalf of Exec)
